study_identification_part.si4_title: Heterogeneity of morphometric similarity networks in health and schizophrenia

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: Apply longitudinal normative modeling to regional morphometric similarity to quantify individual deviations and their changes over time in schizophrenia versus healthy controls, and assess group differences at baseline and follow-up.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: At baseline, SZ showed reduced morphometric similarity in the default mode network and increased in somatomotor; the proportion of individuals with infra/supra-normal deviations per region was low (<6%) in both groups; longitudinal within-person changes in outlier counts were minimal (<1) and not different between groups; normative modeling improved group-level sensitivity versus raw MS.
